Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Partner Ops), Markus Vela (QuantumGrid Head of Cloud Partnerships), Lina Torres (QuantumGrid Solutions Architect), Diego Morales (QuantumGrid BD)

Summary (auto-gen, may miss nuance): Intro / partner alignment: discuss go-to-market (reseller vs referral), technical integration patterns (VPC peering, private control plane, on-prem options), capacity profiles and benchmark plan, initial commercial thoughts and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um i'm alex from redwood, i'm the partner lead on this side, i'll let priya introduce the technical bits but uh really excited to talk through how quantumgrid and redwood might work together.
[00:15] Markus Vela: thanks alex, yeah super excited. quick context on our side, we run a managed GPU cloud focused on enterprise HPC and ML workloads, we're starting to get inbound for large LLM inference and looking for partner models and inference stacks to offer as managed endpoints.
[00:30] Priya Rao: great, thanks markus. i'm priya, systems engineer on the inference team. quick agenda: 1) high level go-to-market and partner models, 2) integration patterns (hosted API vs dedicated vs private), 3) capacity/pricing signals and benchmark plan, 4) security/compliance checklist. sound ok?
[00:45] Lina Torres: sounds good. and diego will be taking notes on the business side.
[00:53] Diego Morales: yep.
[01:05] Alex Chen: cool. first question for you markus — are you thinking reseller where quantumgrid would resell redwood-hosted endpoints, or are you wanting to embed the redwood runtime into your managed offering (dedicated/private)? or a mix?
[01:22] Markus Vela: great question. short term we like reseller/referral — lower ops friction — but long term we want a powered-by model where customers can pick redwood runtime inside quantumgrid console. basically a mix.
[01:37] Alex Chen: that aligns with what other partners have done. we can enable both — hosted API for quick go-to-market, and dedicated/private for customers who want isolated capacity and private control plane. there are slightly different commercial models for each.
[01:50] Priya Rao: technical follow-up — when you say embed, are you expecting VPC peering and private control plane, or fully on-prem? what's your typical customer network setup?
[02:05] Markus Vela: most customers are cloud-hosted in our regions, they want VPC peering and KMS integration. a few regulated clients want air-gapped on-prem instances though that's less common.
[02:20] Priya Rao: ok good. from redwood's side we support three patterns: 1) hosted endpoint (our control plane, easiest to integrate via API key), 2) dedicated (reserved GPU pools in your VPC with peering + private routing), 3) private deployment (we ship a package or support a private control plane). all support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs.
[02:45] Lina Torres: can you clarify the networking for dedicated? like does traffic route through redwood public endpoints or is it fully within customer/partner network?
[02:58] Priya Rao: for dedicated when deployed into partner/customer VPC we can run the inference runtime in their network; requests stay in-network. there's an optional control-plane peering if you want the management plane to be customer-controlled; we also support mutual TLS and SAML for admin. sometimes that wording gets messy in docs, sorry the auto-docs had a small typo last week.
[03:20] Markus Vela: ok that helps. performance is a big ask — our sales teams ask about p99 latency and throughput for common LLMs. what's your guidance and can we run sample benchmarks?
[03:35] Priya Rao: yes. we typically profile models across sequence lengths and batch sizes; we have an internal benchmark harness and can share a spreadsheet. for example, an 8xA100 setup with quantized model yields X tokens/sec and p99 latencies that are competitive with on-prem. (note: numbers vary by model and sequence length). we'd like to run your capacity profile — can you share a typical instance type and network topology for a pilot?
[03:55] Markus Vela: we'll share. our offering uses 8xA100 per instance, NVLink enabled network, customers sometimes want multi-tenant isolation.
[04:10] Alex Chen: perfect. next commercial question — revenue share vs referral. some partners prefer simple reseller margin (flat discount) to start; others want co-sell revenue split. we can be flexible. what's your preference?
[04:25] Diego Morales: from quantumgrid side, we'd want something simple to start (reseller) so our sales motions can be quick. if we see traction we can evaluate a revenue share or dedicated capacity commit.
[04:40] Alex Chen: makes sense. we'll propose a starter reseller discount band in the partner one-pager.
[04:45] Jordan Lee: (partner ops) i'll also share our partner enablement kit — sales decks, technical onboarding checklist, and suggested pricing guidance.
[04:55] Lina Torres: regarding security/compliance: do you have SOC 2 Type II, and can you provide encryption at rest with KMS integration? some of our customers require key management in their cloud KMS.
[05:10] Priya Rao: yes we are SOC 2 and support KMS/HSM. for private deployments we can integrate a customer-managed KMS; for hosted we offer BYOK patterns and audit logs. we'll attach our SOC2 and security pack.
[05:25] Markus Vela: good. on SLAs — do you have latency/uptime SLAs for hosted vs dedicated?
[05:32] Alex Chen: hosted has standard best-effort for free-tier, and SLA-backed targets for paid tiers; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets per contract. exact numbers depend on commit level.
[05:44] Priya Rao: also note fallback routing — if a dedicated pool is overloaded we can fall back to compatible model variants or hosted endpoints to preserve availability; useful for burst patterns.
[05:58] Markus Vela: hmm that fallback behavior could be important for our customers. do you allow customers to opt-out of fallback? some regulated clients don't want data leaving their VPC.
[06:12] Priya Rao: yes opt-out is supported; we can restrict fallback and enforce strict isolation.
[06:20] Alex Chen: ok moving to integration timeline — if quantumgrid wants to start with reseller (hosted), and run a pilot with dedicated validation, what's a realistic timeframe?
[06:33] Markus Vela: our first pilot customers are looking to start in Q3. so if we can get a pilot ready by late July that'd be ideal.
[06:42] Alex Chen: doable. immediate milestones: 1) exchange partner NDA and partner one-pager, 2) run capacity questionnaire and initial benchmark, 3) technical deep dive with infra team, 4) pilot agreement.
[06:58] Diego Morales: for the benchmark, what telemetry do you need? and do you require synthetic traffic or can we replay real requests?
[07:08] Priya Rao: we prefer a synthetic harness that mimics your traffic — sequence length distribution, average batch sizes, request QPS. replay is ok if PII is scrubbed and it matches production distribution. we'll send a questionnaire.
[07:22] Markus Vela: ok we'll prepare sequence length histograms and avg batch sizes.
[07:30] Alex Chen: thanks. competitive landscape — anything we should know about other vendors you're evaluating?
[07:38] Markus Vela: we have early discussions with lambda labs and paperspace; also some customers ask about aws inferentia and nvidia's managed offerings. main differences are ease of integration and partner economics.
[07:50] Alex Chen: good to know. we'll make sure to highlight where Redwood's strengths are — unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, clear ops/observability, and cost/perf tuning.
[08:02] Lina Torres: small clarifying Q: how does billing work for reseller if we resell hosted endpoints? do you do per-token billing to us or direct invoicing to the end customer?
[08:14] Jordan Lee: couple of options: 1) white-label billing where quantumgrid invoices the customer and we invoice quantumgrid (reseller flow); or 2) direct-billing with a referral kickback. we can pick whichever is easier to operationalize initially.
[08:28] Diego Morales: reseller sounds better to start. we can handle support triage and then escalate to redwood for infra issues.
[08:36] Alex Chen: makes sense. for support model we'll outline escalation matrix in the partner kit.
[08:44] Priya Rao: tech note: for dedicated/private customers that want low p99 we recommend enabling prefix caching and KV cache for chat workloads; small config changes can give large perf gains.
[08:58] Markus Vela: interesting — does that change correctness? our customers are sensitive to hallucinations and quality.
[09:08] Priya Rao: prefix caching is safe for exact-match prefixes; quality is unchanged, it's more an inference optimization. we also provide quantization profiles that keep quality within acceptable delta. we'll share eval examples.
[09:22] Alex Chen: ok i think we're near the end — are there any unresolved blockers?
[09:28] Lina Torres: just the benchmark spreadsheet and security docs.
[09:32] Markus Vela: plus the commercial model for reseller margins — a number range would help.
[09:38] Alex Chen: we'll include a starter margin band in the one-pager and follow up with a draft reseller agreement.
[09:44] Jordan Lee: i'll attach our enablement kit and suggested pricing bands after the call.
[09:50] Priya Rao: i'll own the benchmark and questionnaire.
[09:54] Diego Morales: we'll share topology docs and instance configs.
[10:00] Alex Chen: great. thanks everyone. recap of next steps — alex one-pager + draft reseller, priya benchmark questionnaire + run sample, markus share capacity/topology, jordan share enablement kit. we'll sync on a follow-up tech deep dive week of 6/22.
[10:20] Markus Vela: sounds good, thanks all.
[10:24] Alex Chen: thanks. bye.
